characterization_methods.key_findings: The 15Al alloy aged at 625 °C for 6 h shows a Vickers hardness of 887.2 ± 14.1 HV; at 625 °C and 650 °C the hardness stabilizes between 800 HV and 900 HV with prolonged aging.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Load 9.8 N for 15 s; each sample tested 5 times with the average reported; samples prepared by electrolytic polishing (10 % perchloric acid + 90 % ethanol)
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure Vickers hardness of the aged 15Al alloy and construct hardness evolution curves and contour maps as a function of aging time and temperature

interfaces.interface_notes: New BCC phase and FCC Cu-rich phase form at the interfaces between the β-Mn in the aged ultra-hard Fe-Mn-Al-Cu alloys (b0068); the BCC phase is attributed to enrichment of the BCC-stabilizing element Al around the β-Mn interfaces.
interfaces.phase_evolution: α → α + FCC Cu-rich phase → α-Mn + β-Mn + BCC phase → β-Mn + BCC phase + FCC Cu-rich phase (b0068); at 625 °C the α matrix transforms to β-Mn within just 1 h.

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Fe-35Mn-15Al-5Cu ingot produced by melting high-purity (>99.9%) raw materials in a vacuum induction furnace under an argon atmosphere.
Homogenized ingots hot-rolled into plates 4 mm thick; plates then cut by electrical discharge machining into 10 × 5 × 2 mm³ samples.
Samples solution treated at 1100 °C for 10 min under an argon atmosphere, followed by oil quenching.
Solution-treated samples aged at 625 °C for 6 h, followed by water quenching. This condition gives the 15Al alloy a Vickers hardness of 887.2 ± 14.1 HV (Table 2).

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Vickers microhardness measured with an HVS-1000 digital microhardness tester at a load of 9.8 N for 15 s; each sample tested 5 times and the average reported; samples electrolytically polished (10 % perchloric acid + 90 % ethanol).

precipitates.distribution: within the β-Mn / at β-Mn interfaces

structures.overall_structure: After aging at 625 °C for 6 h the 15Al (Fe-35.2Mn-15.0Al-5.2Cu) alloy has an almost fully transformed β-Mn matrix (the α→β-Mn transformation completes within 1 h at ≥600 °C), with abundant fine BCC and FCC Cu-rich precipitates associated with the β-Mn.

unmapped_findings: In the 15Al alloy, aging at 625 °C and 650 °C stabilizes the Vickers hardness between 800 HV and 900 HV with prolonged aging time; the 625 °C/6 h value (887.2 ± 14.1 HV) lies within this plateau (b0037).
The optimal aging temperature range for achieving ultra-high hardness in the 15Al alloy is mainly 525 °C–600 °C, so the 625 °C aging condition lies above the optimal window for this alloy (b0038).
